approvedUseCase.population: USDA/CPER yearling steers in grazing systems
approvedUseCase.scopeNote: The observational case definition does not establish that the current engine represents this population or that its inputs and outputs are jointly observed.

sourcesOfUncertainty.reason: No instrument error, repeatability, or protocol coverage estimates are available for the simulated fields and target population.
Engine constants are illustrative point assumptions and have not been fit to an eligible calibration cohort.
Some public cohorts contain repeated animal observations and can describe within-cohort metric variability, but do not identify the target engine prediction distribution.
Available cohorts do not provide enough independent, compatible clusters across the approved domain to estimate transportable variation.
ADG and DMI diagnostics exist for selected cohorts, but they omit aligned management inputs and the joint outputs required to evaluate the full simulation.
Coverage of the engine input domain and target population is not established; missing inputs cannot be converted into an uncertainty distribution.

outcomes.compatibleIndependentEvidence: Partial component evidence: USDA/CPER temporal holdout and CPER-to-CGRE external transfer; separate Zenodo adult-cow and other cohort diagnostics. New CPER 2009–2013 year-held-out comparison is internal development evidence only; no candidate passed its advancement rule and it is not independent transport validation.
estimableNow: descriptive error and bias for the exact audited cohort and frozen component rule
cluster-bootstrap stability of selected error metrics where animal IDs support it
Descriptive pooled and year-block error and bias for raw endpoint ADG in the exact CPER yearling-steer cohort under the frozen internal protocol; not a probabilistic prediction distribution.
notEstimableNow: transferable interval coverage across years, farms, regions, or populations
adult-cow prediction uncertainty from yearling cohorts
keyLimitations: engine inputs and management are not jointly aligned with observations
observational ADG is not the same estimand as all engine weight outputs
empirical coverage varied across held-out site/year subsets
The frozen internal CPER year-held-out comparison did not advance a candidate and has only five year blocks; no nominal interval coverage is justified.

uncertaintyBySource.reason: Measurement error and repeatability are not reported for the compatible target inputs and outcomes.
Engine constants remain illustrative and no eligible calibration fit is available.
Observed cohorts describe sample variability, but do not identify the engine prediction distribution.
Available evaluations do not support transportable variability across independent target clusters.

ADG component diagnostics exist, but aligned inputs and full-engine outputs are absent. The new five-year CPER internal CV permits only cohort-specific descriptive error; no candidate passed and no independent uncertainty calibration is available.
Target-domain coverage and aligned management inputs are not established.

outcomes.compatibleIndependentEvidence: Component checks exist in feedlot, hay, and dairy grazing cohorts; these are distinct systems and populations from the approved USDA/CPER case.
estimableNow: descriptive component error and bias for each exact dataset, protocol, and frozen rule
notEstimableNow: forage intake uncertainty in the approved target population
joint intake and weight prediction uncertainty
keyLimitations: some sources have small cluster counts or derived outcomes
DMI results cannot be pooled across domains as one distribution

uncertaintyBySource.reason: The available protocols and populations differ, and their measurement-error estimates do not support the target population.
No eligible target-domain calibration cohort or fitted parameter distribution is available.
Some cohorts permit within-cohort descriptions, not a target engine prediction distribution.
The small and heterogeneous cluster counts do not support transportable variation.
Component diagnostics exist in distinct systems, but do not evaluate the full target simulation.
The available cohorts do not establish input coverage for the approved target population.

outcomes.compatibleIndependentEvidence: Some public sources report pasture or vegetation indicators at group, paddock, or remote-sensing level; they are not aligned to the engine's initial stock, daily growth, intake, and paddock transitions. New adjacent forage-biomass evidence includes an external Dryad comparison for sampled pre-grazing forage mass; it does not measure initial pasture stock or validate the engine stock state.
estimableNow: source-specific descriptive summaries when the reported unit and period are retained
Source-specific error and bias for harvested quadrat forage mass predicted from matched height in the exact Mendeley and Dryad cohorts; not pasture-stock uncertainty.
notEstimableNow: daily or paddock-level predictive intervals for engine stock
joint stock and animal outcome uncertainty
keyLimitations: complete aligned time series and management inputs are absent
remote-sensing indicators are not direct stock measurements

The Dryad biomass comparison is related but not an identical sampling estimand; 24/64 predictions exceed the 2–56 cm Mendeley height support, all in MOB treatment, so support is confounded with management/year.

uncertaintyBySource.reason: Available vegetation indicators are not direct measurements of the engine stock outputs.
No aligned stock observations support estimating uncertainty in engine growth or transition parameters.
This outcome is paddock or farm pasture stock; individual-animal variation is not its uncertainty unit.
Available sources do not provide compatible independent stock series across the target domain.

Initial stock, growth, intake, and paddock transitions are not jointly observed against the engine. Source-specific error is now described for clipped-quadrat biomass, but this is not the engine pasture-stock output and cannot establish its uncertainty.
Aligned management inputs and target-domain coverage are absent.

outcomes.compatibleIndependentEvidence: No independent dataset is currently identified with comparable per-animal feed quantities, local prices, and cost outcomes aligned to the engine scenario.

keyLimitations: regional and temporal price variation is not observed by the engine

mustFreezeBeforeHoldout: interval construction method and nominal level
evaluationGate.splitPolicy: Keep all observations from an animal in one partition; also hold out farm, year, region, or system when those clusters define intended transfer.
evaluationGate.promotionRule: A prediction interval may be enabled only for the exact outcome and target domain after an independent compatible evaluation supports its stated coverage. Metric bootstrap intervals and deterministic sensitivity ranges do not satisfy this gate.
